lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
- Cut the signal's daily turnover from 34% to 21% with a cost-aware position smoother, keeping 90% of gross returns and lowering estimated slippage by a third.
- Confirmed the forecast gain over the nested HAR-RV baseline with standard Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices.
- Joining 120 microstructure features point-in-time across six venues, deduplicating late prints and versioning each schema, built a feature store the team reused in two later projects.
- Annualized the signal's daily Sharpe ratio by multiplying it by 252 before reporting it to the desk.
- Documented the backtest assumptions, transaction-cost model and known failure regimes in the desk's research wiki, which the next intern cohort used to onboard in their first week.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Built the lab's simulation pipeline on the shared cluster, cutting a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours, with every run reproducible from its seed and configuration file.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.

- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation while maintaining the lab's shared cluster, organizing the weekly reading group and grading for two courses, which was downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Cut forecast error from 0.20 to 0.15, a 33% improvement, by adding realized-volatility features and an asymmetric loss.
- Improved the model's directional hit rate by 6% on 30 equity indices, from 52% to 58%, with a temporal convolutional model.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Placed 41st of 2,900 teams with a gradient-boosting ensemble on 300 engineered features, finishing in the top 2% of the private leaderboard.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Wrote the team's feature-selection script using permutation importance, trimming 900 candidate features to 300 without losing validation score.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Move the bakery role to Additional Experience or reduce it to one bullet so Northpeak and the other quant evidence receive priority.
items.because: Its current prominence may obscure the professional narrative for quant recruiters.

items.says: Verify that the chronology of the bakery role, Ph.D., and quant career path is accurate.
items.because: Recruiters may wonder how the current bakery role fits with the Ph.D. and quant path.

items.says: Consider adding a Publications or Research section for the JASA submission and other public research output.
items.because: The mathematical contribution is more useful than its current placement under the assistantship.

items.says: Separate teaching into its own entry if it was formally a teaching assistant role.
items.because: It may not belong under the research assistantship.

items.says: Make clear that the independent volatility project is separate from the Northpeak internship.
items.because: The shared HAR-RV baseline, 30 indices, and similar language could suggest duplication or reuse of confidential work.

items.says: Ensure the independent project does not expose employer data, methods, or results.
items.because: Parts of the project may overlap with the internship work.

items.says: Standardize date punctuation and use en dashes consistently.
Replace the placeholder phone number, email, and URL with real contact details in the final version.
Make the code link open directly to a polished GitHub profile or portfolio.
items.because: It should not require additional navigation.

items.says: Add LinkedIn only if the profile is complete and consistent with the résumé.
Remove the code portfolio if it is weak or inactive.
items.because: An underdeveloped profile can hurt more than help.

items.says: Use “candidate” only if formal candidacy has been reached; otherwise use the degree-program designation.
Consider adding the research area, dissertation topic, or advisor.
items.because: That information may be directly relevant to quant roles.

items.says: Verify that the expected graduation date is accurate and consistent across applications.
Add honors or GPA only if they are strong and useful.
Shorten the B.S. line if space becomes tight.
items.because: The Ph.D. carries more weight.

items.says: Change “labour” to “labor.”
items.because: The résumé is U.S.-based.

items.says: Quantify the size or difficulty of the budget achievement.
items.because: “Within budget” only indicates that a requirement was met.

items.says: Give this routine shift responsibility less space than the high-value quantitative work.
Clarify that both 12% and 7% are percentages of production and define the measurement period.
Describe the change consistently as either five percentage points or about a 42% relative reduction.
items.because: The two types of change should not be blurred.

items.says: Clarify whether the Sharpe improvement applies to the signal, a combined backtest, or the actual desk book.
items.because: “Desk book’s Sharpe ratio” suggests a live result while the line says the result came from a backtest.

items.says: Confirm that “out-of-sample” is technically accurate and that the 18-month period was not repeatedly used for model selection.
Ensure the Sharpe figures use the correct annualization methodology.
items.because: The résumé later annualizes daily Sharpe incorrectly.

items.says: Define turnover according to the desk’s convention.
items.because: Turnover definitions vary.

items.says: Clarify whether the one-third slippage reduction came from realized trading or a transaction-cost model.
State the comparison point for “keeping 90% of gross returns.”
items.because: The reviewer suggests the unsmoothed strategy as the likely comparison.

items.says: Remove “standard” unless the exact testing procedure can be defended.
Recheck whether the Diebold–Mariano test is valid for the nested-model comparison.
items.because: Standard DM inference can be problematic in nested settings.

items.says: Name the forecast metric being tested.
items.because: “Forecast gain” is too vague for a technical audience.

items.says: Account for serial dependence, cross-index dependence, and multiple comparisons when claiming significance across 30 indices.
Check whether “30 indices” is consistent with the earlier reference to liquid index futures.
Restructure the sentence to lead with the feature store and use the technical details as support.
items.because: The long introductory phrase delays the main action and makes ownership harder to follow.

items.says: Clarify whether the feature store was built independently or as part of a team.
Verify that “six venues” is plausible for the instruments described elsewhere.
Multiplying daily Sharpe by 252 is mathematically wrong.
items.because: Conventional annualization uses the square root of the number of periods, subject to return-dependence assumptions.

items.says: Delete the Sharpe annualization bullet even if the calculation is corrected.
items.because: Routine reporting is not a résumé-worthy accomplishment.

items.says: Clarify or soften the claimed onboarding impact.
items.because: The wording may imply that the documentation alone caused onboarding to take one week.

items.says: Specify the main source of the simulation speedup if available.
items.because: Technical reviewers will care whether it came from parallelization, vectorization, scheduling, caching, or another method.

items.says: Ensure the three-day and five-hour measurements used comparable hardware and workload.
Remove the first-person phrase “my proof.”
items.because: It is inconsistent with the rest of the résumé.

items.says: Emphasize the mathematical contribution rather than saying it is Section 3.
items.because: The section number is less useful than the result itself.

items.says: Verify that “under review at JASA” is current and update it when the status changes.
Avoid implying sole ownership if the variance-bound result was collaborative.
Add response-count or departmental context for the 4.8/5 rating if available.
items.because: Otherwise the rating may appear selectively reported.

items.says: Treat this teaching bullet as lower priority if space is tight.
items.because: Research and engineering achievements are more important for an industry résumé.

items.says: Split the R-package achievement from the unrelated service responsibilities.
items.because: Combining four responsibilities dilutes a strong software achievement.

items.says: Keep the package and download metric together with an unambiguous referent.
items.because: It is currently unclear what “which was downloaded 3,000 times” refers to.

items.says: Remove or heavily reduce cluster maintenance if it duplicates the simulation-pipeline bullet.
Remove reading-group organization and grading unless leadership or teaching is central to the target role.
Verify the source and definition of the 3,000 downloads.
items.because: Package counts can include automated mirrors or CI systems.

items.says: Add a repository, paper, or technical-report link if the project is public and polished.
State the project’s current output or status.
items.because: It has been ongoing since January 2024.

items.says: Clarify the evaluation period, forecast horizon, and aggregation method if space permits.
Ensure the HAR-RV baseline was tuned and evaluated fairly.
items.because: Technical interviewers may examine this common benchmark closely.

items.says: Confirm that “30 equity indices” is the correct asset description.
The reduction from 0.20 to 0.15 is 25%, not 33%.
Name the forecast-error metric.
items.because: Raw numbers have little meaning without scale and definition.

items.says: Clarify whether this is a separate experiment from the 7% QLIKE result.
Remove the bullet if it merely restates the preceding result with another metric.
items.because: It should add a distinct insight.

items.says: Do not attribute the gain jointly to the features and asymmetric loss without an ablation study.
items.because: Their effects have not been separated.

items.says: Describe the move from 52% to 58% as six percentage points, not 6%.
items.because: The relative increase is approximately 11.5%.

items.says: Define what “directional” means for volatility forecasting.
Avoid repeating the temporal convolutional model and 30-index scope.
items.because: Those facts are already established directly above.

items.says: State whether 58% is statistically distinguishable from 50%.
items.because: Otherwise the number may not be persuasive.

items.says: Keep the directional-accuracy result only if it matters to the strategy or research objective.
Use the competition’s exact official name if it can be disclosed.
Add a Kaggle profile or competition link.
items.because: It would verify the result.

items.says: Verify that 2,900 is the final number of eligible teams rather than total registrations.
Make explicit that 41st was the private or final leaderboard placement.
items.because: The current wording only partly makes that clear.

items.says: Rephrase the claim that time-grouped folds cut validation leakage.
items.because: Closing a local-to-leaderboard gap shows better validation alignment but does not itself prove that leakage was eliminated.

items.says: Explain the time-grouping unit if it can be stated briefly and is technically important.
Identify the score scale for the 0.02 gap.
items.because: The gap may otherwise be hard to interpret.

items.says: Ensure permutation importance did not use the final holdout or private-leaderboard feedback.
Ensure “without losing validation score” refers to a genuinely untouched validation set.
items.because: It should not reflect repeated tuning on the same folds.

items.says: Treat this bullet as lower priority if space is tight.
items.because: It is less distinctive than the placement and leakage-control bullets.

items.says: Reorganize the skills by type.
items.because: Python and R are languages, PyTorch is a framework, and Kafka is data infrastructure.

items.says: Retain Kafka only if there is real hands-on experience to discuss.
items.because: Nothing in the experience section currently supports it.

items.says: Add SQL, Git, Linux, cloud, or cluster technologies only when there is genuine working proficiency.
Correct “econometircs” to “econometrics.”
Ensure every listed method is supported by an experience or project bullet.
Consider adding demonstrated methods such as volatility forecasting, market microstructure, Monte Carlo simulation, or statistical testing.
items.because: They may be more relevant to the target roles.

items.says: Move “gradient boosting” to a modeling-techniques category.
items.because: It fits there better than under broad statistical methods.
